auto-bbc17d97373c.headline: Car bomb in St. Petersburg kills a Russian air forces colonel
auto-bbc17d97373c.summary: A senior Russian military officer died after an explosive device detonated under his car in the Pushkinsky district of St. Petersburg early Thursday, around 7 a.m. local time. Russia's Investigative Committee has opened a criminal case and said all circumstances are being established. Local outlets reported he was a colonel in the Aerospace Forces' 6th Guards Air and Air Defense Forces Army, though his name has not been released. The blast happened about 300 meters from his apartment building, in the Shushary neighbourhood, where another Russian military official was killed by a car explosion in August. Russia has accused Ukraine of several such assassinations, while Ukrainian sources have claimed some attacks and denied others.

actors.why: Senior officer killed in a car bombing on Russian soil, with a criminal probe opened
Russia accuses Ukraine of the killings, which Ukrainian sources partly deny

impact_points: Russia's military is affected by the loss of a senior Aerospace Forces officer in a targeted attack.
Ukraine is implicated by Russian accusations, though the article notes Kyiv has denied involvement in some cases.

auto-e4084dcbb1a8.headline: Trump downplays need for Iran deal and redirects Vance to domestic fraud probe
auto-e4084dcbb1a8.summary: US President Donald Trump said on Thursday that Washington has no need for an agreement with Iran, pointing to money it says it holds and control of the Strait of Hormuz. He asked Vice President JD Vance to concentrate instead on alleged fraud and corruption in Democratic-run cities and states. The move follows a Wall Street Journal report that Vance was weighing face-to-face talks with a senior Iranian security official, which Reuters said it could not confirm. The shift comes after Vance blamed the costly Iran war partly for Republicans' midterm losses and called an earlier recommendation to end the war sound advice.

actors.why: US rejects need for deal, signalling tougher pressure on Tehran
Trump says deal unnecessary and shifts Vance to domestic corruption probe
Regional conflict dynamics shift as diplomacy stalls, though not directly addressed

impact_points: Iran faces a harder US stance, with Trump signalling that talks are not a priority in the eight-month conflict.
Vance's role in peace efforts is sidelined, and his standing as a possible 2028 Republican contender may be affected.

auto-9f28a27ba628.headline: Zelensky urges Europe to guard its interests in US-Russia security talks
auto-9f28a27ba628.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky cautioned European leaders on Thursday against being sidelined by discussions between Washington and Moscow over a possible new security framework for the continent. His remarks reflect concern in Kyiv that decisions about Europe's future could be made without Europe at the table. The report also recalls that Russia, before its 2022 invasion of Ukraine, issued NATO an ultimatum demanding that alliance forces pull back from eastern Europe and that NATO halt new memberships.

actors.why: Kyiv fears being excluded from talks that could shape its security
Moscow gains leverage through direct talks with Washington on security
Washington is central to negotiating a new continental security arrangement
European leaders are urged to be wary of US-Russia discussions

impact_points: Ukraine faces the risk that a US-Russia deal could shape its security without its direct input.
European governments may be pressed to define their own position on continental security arrangements.

auto-3f0ae8797be8.headline: US officer at NATO's UK headquarters held over alleged spying for Russia
auto-3f0ae8797be8.summary: A US Army lieutenant colonel stationed at NATO's Allied Rapid Reaction Corps headquarters in Britain was arrested near Gloucester on suspicion of spying for Russia, according to reporting by the Wall Street Journal citing American officials. The officer, 41, reportedly spoke with people he believed were not state representatives, unaware they were British authorities running a sting operation. British charges are expected next week, with a possible later US court-martial. The Kremlin, through spokesman Dmitry Peskov, denied any link to the officer. British police said the arrest was made with the US Army and the FBI.

actors.why: Arrest on UK soil; British charges expected, enhancing counterintelligence cooperation
Serving officer accused; insider threat and possible US court-martial
Accused of espionage links; Kremlin denies any connection

impact_points: The UK is affected as the arrest took place on its soil and British prosecutors plan an indictment.
NATO and the United States face security concerns over insider access to sensitive information at a key alliance headquarters.

auto-c90777c941b6.headline: Tigray's renewed fighting: is Ethiopia's latest conflict truly over?
auto-c90777c941b6.summary: Fighting between the Tigray People's Liberation Front and Ethiopia's national army resumed in late September, and federal forces entered the regional capital Mekelle within about two weeks. The TPLF withdrew from the city and other main towns, and hundreds are reported dead, including people killed in drone and air strikes. Government supporters say the war is effectively over, while the TPLF calls its retreat a deliberate strategy and says it is preparing a counteroffensive. Residents report continued artillery and drone fighting in parts of the region, and fear is high given past abuses.

actors.why: Federal army retook Mekelle, but clashes and insecurity persist across Tigray
Eritrean soldiers reappeared in Tigray's towns, reviving fears of past atrocities

impact_points: Ethiopia's federal government faces the task of stabilising Tigray amid ongoing clashes and lingering distrust.
Tigray's residents face hunger, lost income and fear, with troops from Ethiopia and Eritrea back in the towns.

auto-e367079686dc.headline: Ukrainian drones hit refinery and plant in southern Russia overnight
auto-e367079686dc.summary:
Overnight on November 12-13, 2026, drones struck an oil refinery in Volgograd and a production site in Rostov-on-Don, according to local officials and Ukrainian monitoring channels. Volgograd's governor confirmed a large attack and fires in the city's southern industrial zone, while Rostov's governor said fires were burning at a production facility and warehouse and that drone debris damaged a residential building. The Volgograd plant, operated by Lukoil and with a capacity of about 15 million metric tons a year, was reportedly hit earlier in October as well. The strikes came a day after trilateral peace talks in Abu Dhabi.

The article notes the attacks fit a Ukrainian campaign against energy infrastructure that supports Russia's military and revenues. Some footage reported to show the refinery on fire could not be independently verified.

actors.why: Refinery fires and fuel queues strain Russia's energy output and civilians.
Ukraine's strikes aim to cut Russian energy revenue and military supply.

impact_points: Russia faces fuel shortages and fuel-related pressure, with Volgograd residents reportedly queuing at gas stations.
Lukoil, Russia's second-largest oil producer, loses output from one of its largest refineries after the strike.

auto-9e9b22ca78bc.headline: Trump warns Mexico of higher tariffs over migrant caravan transit
auto-9e9b22ca78bc.summary: The United States president has threatened to raise tariffs on goods from Mexico in response to large groups of migrants moving north through the country. The warning centres on the caravans and on Mexico's handling of them. The article does not provide further details here, and the scale and timing of any tariff increase were not confirmed in the available material.

actors.why: Faces threatened US tariffs tied to migrant caravan transit
Uses tariff threat as leverage over migration policy
Migrant caravans often originate from Central American countries
Migrant caravans often originate from Central American countries

impact_points: Mexico faces the risk of higher US tariffs on its exports if the migrant flows continue.
The United States could see trade costs rise, since Mexico is one of its largest trading partners.

auto-62a667702033.headline: EU leaders meet in Dublin amid AI, Ukraine and budget disputes
auto-62a667702033.summary: EU leaders gather in Dublin for a summit officially focused on artificial intelligence, though urgent disagreements over Ukraine, the bloc's next budget and the succession at the European Central Bank are also on the agenda. The debate on AI centres on whether Europe should build frontier models to compete with American and Chinese developers, or concentrate on applications, with funding as the main obstacle. Divisions also persist over who should represent Europe in any future Ukraine peace talks, and over how to cover Kyiv's projected funding gap of 70 billion euros next year. Officials expect no major breakthrough, with the next key deadlines falling later in November.

actors.why: Hosts the summit in Dublin, gaining diplomatic visibility
Faces a 70 billion euro shortfall and uncertain peace-talk representation
Europe seeks a unified voice in talks with Moscow, adding pressure
Pushes for linking Ukraine funding to the budget, facing resistance
Disagrees with a single EU representative, keeping E3 channels
Envoy's Moscow talks may open European seats at the table

impact_points: Ukraine faces a projected 70 billion euro funding shortfall next year, depending on EU agreement before the November summit.
Germany, France and other member states must narrow budget and representation differences, which could reshape EU influence in peace talks.

auto-d2dc309738c9.headline: Finland reports strike on Russian navy ship in Gulf of Finland
auto-d2dc309738c9.summary: Finland's military says it detected a strike on a Russian warship in the Gulf of Finland area and is monitoring the situation, while stating the country faces no immediate military threat. Details on the attack's origin, location, timing, and casualties were not provided, and it was unclear what caused the strike. Local media reported the ship was a small Russian navy vessel that returned to Saint Petersburg, and Ukraine's Security Service reportedly said it carried out the attack. Separately, US envoys met Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow and then Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Ireland, following talks in the United Arab Emirates that yielded a planned prisoner exchange.

actors.why: Finland's military detected the strike near its waters, raising regional security concerns
A Russian navy warship was reportedly struck and returned to Saint Petersburg
Ukraine's security service reportedly claimed the attack, a notable operational success
Estonia shares the Gulf of Finland and issued shelter warnings amid drones in its airspace
US envoys held shuttle diplomacy and helped secure a planned prisoner exchange

impact_points: Finland faces heightened Baltic security concerns, though its military says it is not under immediate threat.
Russia's navy and Saint Petersburg-area forces suffer a rare strike, while Ukraine claims the operation and US envoys push a prisoner swap.

auto-905689c09bcf.headline: Oil heads for weekly fall as US keeps Iran blockade in place
auto-905689c09bcf.summary: Crude oil prices were on track for a second consecutive weekly decline, with traders responding to word that the United States will maintain its blockade targeting Iran. The move signals that the restrictions are not being eased despite market expectations for some relief. Details beyond the headline could not be verified here, so the exact price levels and the scope of the blockade are not confirmed.

actors.why: Continued US blockade restricts Iran's oil exports and economy
Maintaining the blockade keeps pressure on Iran but risks market and diplomatic costs
Lower oil prices and wider supply shifts pressure Gulf exporter revenues

impact_points: Iran faces continued US restrictions that cut off its ability to export oil and trade.
Global oil markets are affected, as the prolonged blockade keeps supply concerns in play for importers and consumers.

auto-376de1b12a39.headline: Israel's caretaker defence minister rejects need for opposition sign-off on strikes
auto-376de1b12a39.summary:
Israel's caretaker Defence Minister Israel Katz said on Thursday that the army does not need approval from the opposition or any legal authority to carry out strikes in any arena where it operates. His remarks came after Gadi Eisenkot, tasked with forming a new government, met Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for two hours and urged restraint, warning that force without a direct, immediate threat could harm democracy. Netanyahu had repeatedly threatened to resume the war with Iran during the election campaign, and Avigdor Liberman, a senior opposition figure, warned a caretaker government should not drag Israel into war without parliamentary oversight.

Netanyahu and Eisenkot said after their meeting that they would stay in touch. Eisenkot has until December 6 to form a government, extendable to December 20. Neither coalition won a majority in October's polls.

actors.why: Caretaker government's strike authority is contested amid threats against Iran and coalition talks
Faces renewed Israeli threats of strikes after past bombing campaigns on its nuclear efforts
Trump allied with Netanyahu on past strikes but now prioritises diplomacy, with Israel's posture shaping his options

impact_points: Israel faces domestic tension over whether a caretaker government can order military action without parliamentary oversight.
Iran faces renewed threats of military action from Israel, which has twice bombed its nuclear program with the US.

auto-1bad1774839f.headline: Seized foreign subsidiaries in Russia reportedly fund Kremlin's war drive
auto-1bad1774839f.summary: Russian authorities have put local units of foreign firms under temporary administration, and several of these businesses have reportedly moved billions of rubles to a state-linked fund that buys drones, vehicles and communications gear for troops. Paint maker AkzoNobel is reported to have sent about two billion rubles, while AB InBev Efes, Metro and DKC each reportedly sent one billion. Poland's Can-Pack and Denmark's Rockwool's former Russian unit also reportedly made transfers. The sums are small next to expected 2026 war spending of over 17 trillion rubles, but the payments offer management a way to signal loyalty. Since January 2025, authorities have taken control of assets of more than 20 foreign firms, nearly all European.

actors.why: Seized foreign assets are funnelled into military procurement via a state-linked fund
AkzoNobel lost control of its Russian unit and its money backs the Russian army
Can-Pack's Russian assets were seized and it reportedly transferred 1.5 billion rubles
Rockwool's former Russian unit reportedly transferred 600 million rubles after seizure
AB InBev Efes, Belgian-linked, reportedly sent one billion rubles and did not comment
DKC Europe, Italian-linked, reportedly sent one billion rubles and did not comment

impact_points: European companies such as AkzoNobel, Metro and Can-Pack are losing control of Russian assets while their funds back the war.
Russia gains a modest source of military funding and a way to pressure foreign firms into supporting its authorities.

auto-af8e7f234ecf.headline: Drone strike on Rivne apartment block leaves six injured, including two children
auto-af8e7f234ecf.summary: A drone hit a residential high-rise in Rivne, western Ukraine, overnight on 12-13 November, starting fires in two flats. Rivne Oblast's military administration head, Oleksandr Koval, first reported five injured, then revised the figure to six, two of them children. Emergency services attended and city authorities were preparing to relocate residents. Window replacement and repairs to the building were expected to start in the morning.

actors.why: Civilians injured and homes damaged by Russian drone strike in Rivne
Accused of launching the drone attack on a civilian apartment block

impact_points: Ukraine's residents of Rivne face injuries, displacement and damaged homes after a Russian drone attack on a residential block.
Russia's strikes on civilian housing in western Ukraine continue, deepening the humanitarian toll on Ukrainian families.

auto-778976f3f4af.headline: China's spokesman stresses communication with US military
auto-778976f3f4af.summary: China's foreign ministry spokesperson has said Beijing values strategic communication with the US military. The remarks come as speculation mounts over a possible China-US-Russia summit at the APEC meeting in Shenzhen in November, which some have likened to the 1945 Yalta Conference. Analysts quoted in the piece expect little substantive progress, pointing to divergent interests on Ukraine, nuclear arms, trade and AI, while Europe's exclusion from such talks has drawn criticism.

actors.why: Seeks to project openness to military dialogue while resisting a great-power carve-up
Military communication with Beijing eases tensions but summit prospects remain uncertain
Pushing a security review in talks that Europe may be excluded from
Fears a Yalta-style deal over its territory and future security
Excluded from trilateral talks it sees as shaping its own security

impact_points: China gains a platform to present itself as a champion of multilateralism while managing ties with Washington.
Ukraine and European states risk being sidelined if great powers negotiate security arrangements over their heads.

auto-59c1f0c135d9.headline: Iran claims two tankers burning in Hormuz after striking mines
auto-59c1f0c135d9.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards Navy says two oil tankers caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz after hitting naval mines. The IRGC claims the ships had turned off their tracking systems and tried to leave through an unauthorised route while under the protection of US forces. It says the vessels are still burning and have been abandoned, and it released video of the burning ships. The claims come from the Iranian side and could not be independently verified from this report. The IRGC also disputed US military accounts of the incident.

actors.why: Its navy claims the strikes enforce its rules; faces scrutiny over the incident.
Accused by Iran of escorting violating tankers; disputes Iranian account.

impact_points: Iran is positioning itself as the enforcer of shipping rules in Hormuz, signalling control over a key chokepoint.
The United States is accused by Tehran of backing vessels that broke Iranian-set routes, raising tensions with Washington.

auto-38ad65d5b9bf.headline: Czechia may deliver first Skyfox trainer jets to Ukraine in 2027
auto-38ad65d5b9bf.summary: Czech Foreign Minister Petr Macinka said in a television interview that Czechia could hand over the first four L-39 Skyfox jets to Ukraine in 2027, with eight more expected a year later. The aircraft, built by Aero Vodochody, are mainly pilot trainers but can also be used for light attack, reconnaissance and patrols, which Kyiv sees as a cheaper way to counter Russian drones. Delivery depends on export licences for foreign-made parts from Belgium, France and the United States. Separately, a proposed order of 12 more aircraft, valued at 6 to 8 billion Czech crowns, would be funded internationally rather than from the Czech budget.

actors.why: Gains aircraft to counter Russian drone attacks, if deliveries proceed
Secures a priority manufacturing order for its domestic aerospace firm
Export licences for avionics components could affect the delivery schedule
Export licences for avionics components could affect the delivery schedule
Export licences for avionics components could affect the delivery schedule

impact_points: Ukraine stands to gain cheaper aircraft to help intercept Russian attack drones, though deliveries remain uncertain.
Czechia benefits from a manufacturing order, while Belgium, France and the United States hold export-licence leverage over the timeline.

auto-c0b6d0bd67f0.headline: ASEAN weighs easing Myanmar ban as members deepen bilateral ties
auto-c0b6d0bd67f0.summary:
Southeast Asian bloc ASEAN faces pressure at its November summit in Manila to ease a five-year restriction on Myanmar's military-backed leaders attending high-level meetings. Several members, including Thailand, Laos, Vietnam, Cambodia and Malaysia, have hosted Myanmar's Min Aung Hlaing on official visits this year despite the civil war that has followed the 2021 coup and killed over 100,000 people.

Thailand's foreign minister urged that Myanmar's foreign minister be allowed to attend ASEAN foreign-minister meetings, hoping for a decision by 2028 at the latest. Analysts say the shift strains the Five-Point Consensus, whose implementation has stalled, and Singapore, next year's chair, faces the task of reconciling divergent approaches.

actors.why: Could gain diplomatic recognition if restrictions on its leaders are eased.
Leading re-engagement push, motivated by border fighting and trade concerns.
Must reconcile divergent member approaches as next year's chair.
Pledged to work towards Myanmar's reintegration into the bloc.
Hosting the Manila summit and preparing a document reviewing implementation.

impact_points: Myanmar's military-backed leadership could gain wider diplomatic recognition if ASEAN lifts its summit restrictions.
Thailand, facing spillover fighting along its border, is pushing for re-engagement while Singapore must reconcile the bloc's divided approaches.

auto-da66abe16c52.headline: Iran's parliament speaker says Washington must respond on peace talks
auto-da66abe16c52.summary: Iran's parliament speaker, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, told Al Jazeera that Tehran does not want the war with the United States to continue and that Washington now needs to act on peace negotiations. He said Iran has already sent a clear set of demands, but the Trump administration has not replied. Ghalibaf said a deal remains possible if it respects earlier understandings and avoids steps that erode trust. He also accused the US of a siege that restricts food, trade and healthcare access, and said Iran aims to end the current limbo between war and peace through talks or deterrence.

actors.why: Faces trade and healthcare restrictions, yet Tehran is pressing for talks it presents as its offer.
Under pressure to answer Iran's demands; no reply yet to the proposal.

impact_points: Iran faces continued economic hardship from restricted food, trade and healthcare access, which Tehran blames on Washington.
The United States must decide whether to respond to Iran's demands, shaping whether talks or continued hostility follow.

auto-7199aa1e435b.headline: Houthis claim drone and missile attacks on Saudi sites as UN extends Yemen sanctions
auto-7199aa1e435b.summary:
Saudi-led coalition forces said they intercepted suspected Houthi drones over the Riyadh region and the Eastern Province. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree claimed strikes on oil infrastructure, including a pumping station on the East-West Pipeline and the Yanbu facility on the Red Sea, as well as military targets. Riyadh says it has rerouted about 4 million barrels of crude daily through the pipeline to Yanbu. On the same day, the UN Security Council unanimously renewed Yemen sanctions for another year and condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.

Separately, Saudi Arabia is reportedly lobbying the EU to label the Houthis a terrorist organisation, a move European officials worry could hurt future peace efforts.

actors.why: Drone and missile attacks on oil sites and military bases; pipeline rerouting strain
Civilian displacement and ongoing fighting across frontlines
Pressed to designate Houthis as terrorists while weighing peace process risks
China's envoy backed de-escalation and called sanctions a means, not an end

impact_points: Saudi Arabia faces attacks on oil infrastructure and a drive to rebuild pipeline export routes.
The EU is caught between Saudi pressure to list the Houthis and concerns about derailing peace talks.

auto-3f3bc55ed9af.headline: IAEA voices growing alarm over Iran's undisclosed enrichment site at Isfahan
auto-3f3bc55ed9af.summary: The United Nations nuclear watchdog says it is increasingly worried about a uranium enrichment plant at Isfahan that Iran declared last year but has not allowed inspectors to visit. In a confidential report to member states, reported on Friday, the International Atomic Energy Agency says it does not know the plant's exact location, status, or whether it holds nuclear material. Iran has also kept inspectors away from facilities struck during last June's 12-day bombing campaign by Israel and the United States. The agency calls the lack of access to Iran's stock of highly enriched uranium a serious proliferation concern.

actors.why: Faces IAEA pressure and proliferation concern over blocked inspections and unknown uranium stocks
Its strikes on Iranian sites leave the status of enriched uranium unverified
Joint strikes on Iran leave its nuclear material unaccounted for, complicating verification
Vienna hosts the IAEA, whose board is reviewing Iran's safeguards non-compliance

impact_points: Iran faces mounting pressure from the IAEA over blocked access to its nuclear sites and stockpile.
Israel and the United States, which carried out the strikes, face continued uncertainty about the state of Iran's enrichment programme.

auto-2e7a26f3aa43.headline: Iran reportedly hits navigation systems on Omani island in Hormuz
auto-2e7a26f3aa43.summary: Three sources told Reuters that Iran attacked ship navigation systems on Didamar, an Omani island in the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian state media said the Revolutionary Guard Corps destroyed enemy navigation equipment there. The sources gave no damage assessment, and Reuters could not independently confirm whether systems were destroyed, though smoke was visible. Two shipping sources said the impact on commercial traffic would likely be limited because other systems operate elsewhere. Gulf oil exports have recovered to over 80% of pre-war levels, helped by US-assisted transit and Saudi flows through Yanbu.

Revolutionary Guard claims strikes on enemy navigation systems, showing reach
US military aids shipping through Hormuz; attacks challenge that effort
Fujairah ship-to-ship transfers depend on Hormuz flows that are threatened
Saudi exports via Yanbu help offset Hormuz disruption, which this attack threatens

impact_points: Oman faces a strike on its own territory, with navigation infrastructure used for Gulf oil flows hit.
Gulf oil exporters and shippers depend on Hormuz workarounds that this attack could further disrupt.

auto-6299c841d45e.headline: Trump says no Iran deal needed as Vance is redirected to domestic probes
auto-6299c841d45e.summary: US President Donald Trump has said Washington does not need a deal with Iran and has told Vice President JD Vance to concentrate on alleged corruption in Democrat-run cities and states. Vance, who led earlier negotiations and has criticised the war, has argued it cost Republicans their congressional majorities. The article notes that Iran said it struck a US early-warning radar in Bahrain, calling it retaliation for a strike on a telecom tower in Sirik. auto-e89fd32fa879.headline: Israeli strike hits Gaza's Nasser hospital, killing six and wounding dozens
auto-e89fd32fa879.summary: Six people were reported killed and around 30 wounded after an overnight Israeli air strike on Nasser hospital in Khan Younis, southern Gaza, according to Hamas-run health authorities. The hospital's director said two missiles struck a surgical building, with one failing to detonate. Among the dead was a surgeon, Dr Rizq Abu Shaira. The Israeli military said it targeted a Hamas brigade commander and fighters it claimed were using the site as a base; the hospital denied receiving any warning. The claims could not be independently verified because international media are barred from entering Gaza.

Military claims the strike removed a threat, but faces criticism over a hospital attack

auto-2e9b8a66d86c.headline: Iran claims strike on US radar site in Bahrain after Sirik incident
auto-2e9b8a66d86c.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say they targeted a US early-warning radar in Bahrain, framing it as retaliation for an attack on a telecommunications tower in the southern port city of Sirik, Hormozgan province. Iranian state media said Sirik was hit by enemy fire on Thursday. The IRGC warned it would respond without limits if such actions continued, citing aerial provocations and oil smuggling in the Strait of Hormuz. Neither Washington nor Manama had commented at the time, and the claim could not be independently confirmed. Bahrain hosts the US Navy's Fifth Fleet headquarters, which was struck earlier in the conflict.

actors.why: Launched retaliatory strike claim, but risks escalation and further retaliation

Military assets in region targeted; troops reduced and diplomatic staff ordered out
Security cabinet ordered preparations for possible attack on Iran

Iran faces the risk of further US or Israeli retaliation as both sides escalate rhetoric and military preparations.

auto-1dcd642dd684.headline: US envoys to visit Moscow and Dublin after Abu Dhabi talks on Ukraine
auto-1dcd642dd684.summary: Trilateral talks between Russia, Ukraine and the United States in Abu Dhabi ended after two days without any breakthrough toward ending the war. Both Moscow and Kyiv confirmed that a large prisoner exchange is being prepared and could happen soon. US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are due to meet Vladimir Putin in Moscow and then Volodymyr Zelensky in Dublin. Territory, especially the Donetsk region, remains the hardest issue, and Europe's role in any security framework is still disputed.

Pushes territorial demands and a limit on NATO influence in eastern Europe
Mediating and pushing for a prisoner swap and a broader framework
Excluded from direct talks but seeking a role in any security arrangement

European states, including those in eastern Europe, remain sidelined from talks but see their security tied to Ukraine's outcome.

auto-0ea97a189593.headline: IAEA presses Iran to restore nuclear site inspections
auto-0ea97a189593.summary: The UN nuclear watchdog, the IAEA, has asked Iran to let its inspectors return to nuclear facilities, according to a report circulated to member states on Friday. Access has been very limited since US and Israeli strikes on Iranian nuclear sites in June 2025. The agency said it lacks information about Iran's atomic sites and nuclear material and called this a proliferation concern, while noting it could resume work at short notice. Iran has pointed to the security situation and to US threats of further attacks as reasons inspections cannot resume yet.

auto-54abeb435828.headline: Woman dies after Russian strike hits bus in Zaporizhzhia region
auto-54abeb435828.summary: A woman who was seriously hurt in a Russian attack on a regular passenger bus in the Zaporizhzhia district of Zaporizhzhia Oblast has died in hospital. The attack took place on 12 November. Mykhailo Semikin, head of the regional military administration, announced the death and said doctors had tried to save her but could not.

actors.why: Civilian bus attack in Zaporizhzhia Oblast killed a woman; reported by Ukrainian officials.

Residents who rely on regular bus services in the region face continuing safety risks from attacks.

auto-007dfc9f5122.headline: German drone maker reports cyberattack; military fleet reportedly grounded then returned to service
auto-007dfc9f5122.summary:
Quantum Systems, a Bavarian firm that supplies drones to Ukraine's military, says it detected a cybersecurity incident in late October and was targeted by hostile actors. The company says its IT and security teams contained the attack and that the systems pose no risk to users or operators, with an investigation ongoing.

The Financial Times reported that the German armed forces had temporarily taken the company's drones out of service as a precaution, a claim the Defence Ministry declined to comment on. The article's headline indicates the drones are flying again.

auto-03db469ebbab.headline: Pakistan says 43 militants killed in northwest raids after police attack
auto-03db469ebbab.summary: Pakistan's military says it killed 43 militants in raids on their hideouts in the country's northwest. The operations followed an attack by gunmen on police officers in Kohat district of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, which left 10 officers and 18 fighters dead and 12 police wounded, according to provincial police. The Pakistani Taliban later claimed responsibility for the ambush. Officials said the fighters were targeted in a separate operation in the Orakzai area of Kohat, where weapons were seized. Pakistan blames the Pakistani Taliban for rising violence, which it says is launched from Afghanistan.

auto-de7c41897e8d.headline: US envoys press Ukraine peace talks as Starlink restrictions and territory dispute persist
auto-de7c41897e8d.summary: US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met Vladimir Putin in Moscow after talks in Abu Dhabi, then travelled to Dublin to meet Ukraine's President Zelensky. Witkoff said another trilateral round had been agreed and that European partners would join it. Zelensky reported that Ukraine faced fresh restrictions on Starshield, the military-grade Starlink service, making it harder to intercept Russian drones, and said Kyiv was seeking clarity from Washington. Putin maintained that the state border must be the only dividing line, with no discussion of contested zones, and proposed localised ceasefires. Ukraine has not agreed to them.

actors.why: Starlink restrictions hinder drone interception and peace terms demand territory Kyiv rejects
Putin holds firm on border demands while US engagement advances Moscow's security framing
US envoys drive talks but face tension over Starshield and Ukrainian territorial concerns
European partners are set to join talks on a security framework affecting their interests
UK national security adviser's Dublin participation was delayed, reducing London's role

impact_points: Ukraine faces battlefield disadvantage from Starshield restrictions that hamper intercepting Russian jet-powered drones.
Europe risks being sidelined as the US discusses a new European security order with Russia and Ukraine.

auto-f800ef207473.headline: Leaked database suggests over 450,000 Russian military deaths since 2022
auto-f800ef207473.summary:
A database reportedly taken from Russia's state statistics agency, Rosstat, records more than 450,000 Russian military personnel dead since the invasion of Ukraine began in February 2022. The records come from death certificates, and outlets including EL PAÍS, Bloomberg, Mediazona and Meduza said they checked the data against other open sources and found no sign of fabrication. The figures run through late August of this year and exclude people listed as missing, so the true total could be higher. The records also include at least one Spanish citizen and dozens of Latin Americans.

The article notes that some entries are not clearly tied to the fighting and that not all deaths have been confirmed by forensic reports. Analysts say the data broadly supports earlier estimates from independent investigations, which had put the toll well below this level.

actors.why: Leaked data exposes a very large, previously opaque military death toll
Russia's heavy losses are the outcome of fighting against Ukraine
A Spanish citizen killed fighting for Russia has been verified

impact_points: Russia faces a far higher military death toll than officially acknowledged, with implications for its manpower and domestic politics.
Families of foreign nationals, including Spaniards and Latin Americans, who served in Russian forces are also affected by the revelations.

auto-d4971bac9b78.headline: Low turnout at COP31 in Turkey raises doubts about climate ambition
auto-d4971bac9b78.summary: Attendance at the COP31 climate summit in Turkey has been thin, with many seats left empty, a pattern the report links to limited ambition for the talks. The piece also points to contradictions in how the host country approaches climate policy. The coverage frames the gathering against a backdrop of increasingly frequent climate disasters that world leaders routinely cite as a reason for urgent action.

actors.why: Hosting a weakly attended summit exposes its climate contradictions and reputation
European attention is pulled toward Ukraine talks, reducing climate summit focus

impact_points: Turkey, as host, faces reputational pressure over the summit's weak turnout and its own policy contradictions.
Vulnerable countries exposed to climate disasters risk seeing slower progress on the commitments they are seeking.

auto-a1db567a1177.headline: Israeli gunfire kills one in eastern Gaza City as raids hit Nablus
auto-a1db567a1177.summary:
A Palestinian man was killed by Israeli gunfire in the Tuffah area east of Gaza City, according to al-Shifa Hospital. In the occupied West Bank, Israeli troops moved through several neighbourhoods of Nablus and searched homes in the nearby towns of Beit Furik and Beit Dajan. Citing security sources, the Palestinian news agency Wafa said soldiers entered residences in several Nablus districts and camps and disturbed belongings inside them.

The reports describe the incidents as they were relayed by the hospital and Wafa; the details were not independently confirmed in this account.

actors.why: A Palestinian killed in Gaza and homes raided in Nablus and nearby towns
Israeli forces carried out the shooting and the raids in the West Bank

impact_points: Palestinians in Gaza City face lethal fire, with a reported death adding to civilian casualties.
Residents of Nablus and nearby towns face home searches and intrusions by Israeli forces.

auto-1330a782a5a8.headline: Chinese chipmaker SMIC expects AI computing shortage to last to 2028
auto-1330a782a5a8.summary: Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corp, China's largest contract chipmaker, reportedly expects demand for artificial intelligence computing to outstrip supply until 2028. The outlook comes as Nvidia's position in the market is drawing scrutiny, and the article suggests this could prompt tighter restrictions on advanced chip exports. The piece appears to frame the shortage as tied to the broader technology rivalry between Beijing and Washington. The article text was limited, so the full details of the company's forecasts and the policy proposals could not be confirmed.

actors.why: SMIC expects shortages, limiting domestic AI computing capacity through 2028
Possible tighter chip curbs reflect Washington's effort to restrict China's AI progress

impact_points: China's domestic chip industry faces sustained pressure as AI computing demand exceeds available capacity.
Nvidia and U.S. policymakers may face tighter curbs on chip exports to China, affecting supply chains.

auto-23af6fdbfbce.headline: Beirut falafel shop passes from fourth generation as family marks a century of trade
auto-23af6fdbfbce.summary: The Tabbara family has run a falafel shop in Beirut for more than a hundred years, outlasting two world wars and a string of regional conflicts. Mohammed Tabbara, 82, still works the counter in the busy Hamra district, while his 40-year-old son Ziad is preparing to take over the business. The family says its recipe relies on fava beans rather than chickpeas, and customers say they come back for the taste and cleanliness. The report also notes that Lebanon's prolonged economic crisis has made affordable meals like these especially important for many residents.

actors.why: Local business continuity amid long economic and security hardship in Beirut.

impact_points: Lebanon's small businesses and residents feel the pressure of an economic crisis, and affordable food remains vital.
The Tabbara family's shop shows continuity through wars, though the report stresses it is a local story with no direct international consequences.

auto-5be8832931a6.headline: Lula lands in Manila for state visit ahead of ASEAN Summit
auto-5be8832931a6.summary: Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva arrived in Manila on Friday, November 13, for a state visit ahead of the 49th ASEAN Summit. He is the first Brazilian president to make a state visit to the Philippines, travelling with his wife and an official delegation, and was greeted by Transportation Secretary Vince Dizon on behalf of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. The schedule includes a wreath-laying at the Rizal Monument, talks with Marcos at the Philippine International Convention Center, and a signing of bilateral agreements. Lula will attend the summit as guest of the chair from November 15 to 17. The visit also marks 80 years of Philippines-Brazil relations.

actors.why: Lula's state visit deepens ties and secures new bilateral agreements
Hosts Lula and the ASEAN Summit, strengthening bilateral relations as chair

impact_points: Brazil gains closer ties with the Philippines through a first-ever state visit and signed bilateral agreements.
The Philippines, as ASEAN chair, gains a high-profile partner for its regional summit and bilateral diplomacy.

auto-1fc357789d20.headline: Erdogan labels Gaza devastation ecocide at Antalya climate summit
auto-1fc357789d20.summary: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan used the COP31 UN climate summit in Antalya to urge the world to recognise the environmental toll of the Israel-Hamas war in Gaza, calling it ecocide as well as genocide. He pointed to destroyed olive groves, polluted soil and water, and flooded shelters, and asked Israel to allow more aid into the territory. Israel's Foreign Ministry rejected his remarks, accusing him of spreading falsehoods and backing Hamas. Gaza's health authorities say more than 74,000 people have been killed since the offensive began, and a UN report found most farmland and fishing livelihoods have been badly damaged.

actors.why: Flooding, damaged farmland and blocked aid deepen hardship for Gaza's population.
Faces renewed international criticism over Gaza and rejects the ecocide and genocide claims.
Gains a platform to press its anti-Israel stance on the international stage.

impact_points: Palestinians in Gaza face worsening flooding, shelter loss, food insecurity and damaged farmland and fishing livelihoods.
Israel faces sharper international criticism over its conduct in Gaza, while Turkiye uses the forum to press its anti-Israel position.

auto-81d9bc8cb2c3.headline: Iraq's foreign minister warns US-Iran standoff must end in peace or war
auto-81d9bc8cb2c3.summary:
Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein told France 24 that the current state of neither war nor peace between Washington and Tehran is unsustainable. He said Iraq sees itself as a mediator, since it has been drawn into the conflict between Iran and the US and Israel. Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi recently travelled to Tehran to meet Iranian parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf.

Hussein also said Baghdad has not yet carried out a US demand to keep only two border crossings with Iran open, calling it a possible sanction on Iraqi people and saying talks with US officials continue. He added that Iraqi oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz, under US protection, have risen to about 3.2 million barrels a day, and that the government aims to bring armed groups under state control by June 2027.

actors.why: Caught between US demands and Iranian ties; mediating while exports depend on US protection
Iraqi mediation and talks offer Tehran a diplomatic channel amid standoff
Pressing Baghdad on border crossings while protecting Iraqi oil flows through Hormuz

impact_points: Iraq faces pressure from Washington over border closures while its oil exports depend on US-protected Hormuz routes.
Iraqi citizens could bear the cost of border restrictions, which Hussein says would act like a sanction on them.

auto-81424db309e7.headline: Saudi and Chinese officials discuss Houthi threats and regional stability
auto-81424db309e7.summary: Saudi Arabia's foreign minister met with a Chinese envoy to talk about recent Houthi attacks and wider security across the region. The discussion focused on the threat posed by the Yemen-based group and how to keep the area stable. The full details of the meeting, including any commitments made, could not be confirmed from the available material.

actors.why: Faces Houthi attacks and seeks diplomatic backing on regional security
Its envoy engages Gulf partners, gaining diplomatic influence in the region
Houthi attacks and regional pressure keep Yemen's conflict and instability in focus

impact_points: Saudi Arabia faces continued security pressure from Houthi attacks, making diplomatic coordination with partners important.
China is drawn into regional security diplomacy, with its envoy engaging Gulf leaders over shared stability concerns.

auto-902fd61adc03.headline: Pentagon honours soldier who rebuked Hegseth's group at Arlington tomb
auto-902fd61adc03.summary:
The Pentagon says US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth has presented a Joint Service Commendation Medal to Specialist Thomas Iglesias, the sentinel who told Hegseth's group to be quiet at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier during a Veterans Day event at Arlington National Cemetery. Video showed Hegseth, his wife and senior advisers laughing and posing for photos before the rebuke. Chief Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell said the soldier had correctly reminded visitors to keep decorum. Guards at the tomb, who are from the 3rd US Infantry Regiment, reportedly issue such reminders several times a day.

The event also featured President Donald Trump, who praised Hegseth and cited the Iran war as an administration success. An effort to impeach Hegseth over the Iran conflict failed in Congress a day earlier.

actors.why: Hegseth's conduct at the tomb drew scrutiny while the Pentagon publicly backed the guard.

impact_points: Specialist Thomas Iglesias and the Old Guard are recognised for enforcing the tomb's rules of silence and respect.
Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth faces renewed scrutiny over the optics of the ceremony and his conduct of the Iran war.

auto-ea6ab2bc9953.headline: Spanish housing protests turn violent in Madrid and Barcelona during nationwide strike
auto-ea6ab2bc9953.summary: Demonstrations across Spain over housing costs and household purchasing power were held during a nationwide 24-hour strike, the first of its kind since 2012. Authorities estimated around 120,000 people marched in Madrid and more than 50,000 rallied in Barcelona. Scattered clashes followed in both cities, with masked protesters throwing objects at police and setting fires, while officers responded with rubber bullets and tear gas. Police reported at least 73 arrests nationwide from over 1,000 incidents linked to the strike, including blockades and burning rubbish bins. The unrest comes just weeks before an early general election.

actors.why: Domestic unrest and arrests over housing costs weigh on the government ahead of an election

impact_points: Spain's government faces mounting public pressure over housing affordability just weeks before an early general election.
Spanish police and protesters were involved in clashes, with dozens of arrests reported across the country.

auto-d26c9fe59670.headline: Iran says it may use self-defence if attacked by US
auto-d26c9fe59670.summary: Iran's Foreign Minister Seyyed Abbas Araghchi has warned that Tehran retains the right to defend itself if the United States launches military action against it. He argued that any US attack without a valid legal basis would be an internationally wrongful act for which Washington would be responsible, and cited Article 51 of the UN Charter as the basis for Iran's response. Earlier, on November 11, Araghchi criticised US officials, accusing them of baseless assumptions that had caused American policy to fail, and attacked remarks by Marco Rubio and Mike Pompeo. The statements are Iran's position and were not independently verified.

actors.why: Faces threatened US strikes and asserts its right to respond militarily
Warned that any attack without legal basis would be wrongful and carry responsibility

impact_points: Iran faces heightened risk of military confrontation with the United States if threatened attacks materialise.
The United States could face legal accountability claims under international law if it strikes Iran without justification.

auto-cbc949eaf9a5.headline: Moscow pushes wider European security deal as Ukraine talks stall
auto-cbc949eaf9a5.summary: Peace talks over Russia's war in Ukraine have made little headway, while Moscow is pressing for a broader agreement on Europe's security order. US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner held talks with Vladimir Putin in Moscow and then met Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Dublin, after Abu Dhabi discussions yielded only an agreed prisoner exchange. Zelenskyy said Europe's future security arrangements should wait until the war ends and Ukraine receives guarantees, while Estonia's prime minister warned that debating them distracts from securing peace. Russia's chief negotiator Vladimir Medinsky compared the goal to the Yalta and Potsdam conferences.

actors.why: Kyiv seeks guarantees and resists talks on Europe's security before the war ends
Moscow pushes for a wider security deal reflecting its demands on Ukraine
Estonia urges continued European support for Ukraine and more pressure on Russia
US envoys mediate talks and seek progress on territory and a ceasefire
A possible Trump-Putin-Xi meeting in China could give Moscow leverage

impact_points: Ukraine faces pressure over territory and security guarantees while Russia presses for a wider European settlement.
European states, led by Estonia, are urged to keep backing Kyiv and pressure Moscow before discussing Europe's security order.

auto-d9ec862ff577.headline: Indian rupee weakens as oil costs and US yields pressure markets
auto-d9ec862ff577.summary: The Indian rupee fell as higher crude oil prices and rising US bond yields weighed on local stock and bond markets. Traders pointed to the combined pressure from costlier energy imports and stronger returns on US government debt drawing capital away from emerging markets. The move reflects how external price and interest-rate shifts can quickly transmit into currency and asset prices in India. Specific figures were not available for this summary.

actors.why: Rupee weakens and stocks and bonds fall on costlier oil and US yields
Rising Treasury yields reflect strength in the US financial position

impact_points: India is exposed because its heavy oil imports become more expensive, widening pressure on the rupee.
Indian investors and bond holders face losses as US yields rise and draw capital toward American assets.

auto-c047ef0f7490.headline: US envoys press Ukraine peace talks as Starlink access dispute deepens
auto-c047ef0f7490.summary:
US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met Vladimir Putin in Moscow after talks in Abu Dhabi, then travelled to Dublin to meet Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky. Witkoff said another round of trilateral talks had been agreed and that European partners would join. Zelensky reported that Ukraine faces restrictions on Starlink's military Starshield service, which he said hampers intercepts of Russian drones. Putin insisted the state border must be the only dividing line, and proposed local ceasefires for evacuations. Kushner spoke of a new European security framework.

The talks centre on European security arrangements in a post-war scenario, though Moscow's demands on territory and neutrality remain far apart from Kyiv's positions. A UK national security adviser's planned Dublin attendance was called off by Downing Street.

actors.why: Starlink restrictions hinder drone interception; Kyiv resists territorial demands
Putin's demands on territory and neutrality remain unchanged; talks progress with US
Envoys drive talks and seek a new European security framework
Planned participation of national security adviser in Dublin talks was cancelled
Excluded from core security-architecture discussions but invited to next round

impact_points: Ukraine faces hampered drone interception and a dispute over US decisions treating its territory as contested.
Europe risks being sidelined from decisions on its own security order, though Witkoff says European partners will join the next round.

auto-128d476a38a1.headline: Profile of Maryland senator Chris Van Hollen, a potential Senate majority leader bid
auto-128d476a38a1.summary:
Democratic Senator Chris Van Hollen of Maryland has said he will run for Senate majority leader as Democrats prepare to take control of Congress in January after strong midterm results. He framed the bid as a call for new leadership, and Michigan senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed backed him publicly while saying he would not support the current minority leader, Chuck Schumer, for the post. The article profiles Van Hollen, who has served in Congress since 2003, including his family background and his high-profile criticism of Trump-era policy and of US policy toward Israel.

The piece also recounts his involvement in the case of a Maryland man deported to El Salvador and his efforts on Gaza, the West Bank and Israeli military detention of Palestinian children. It notes that a September resolution he forced to a vote failed 47-53.

actors.why: Democrats seek new Senate leadership after midterm gains, shaping congressional direction
Van Hollen's push could bring tighter US scrutiny of Israeli military conduct

impact_points: The Democratic Party's Senate leadership could change, with Van Hollen challenging the incumbent Chuck Schumer for the role.
Israel could face tighter US scrutiny and possible limits on military assistance if Van Hollen gains influence over Senate policy.

auto-a6bdf956777e.headline: Military helicopter crashes near Malatya, killing four Turkish personnel
auto-a6bdf956777e.summary: A Turkish military helicopter came down on Thursday evening in Samankoy, on the southern edge of Malatya province's capital in southern Türkiye, killing four personnel aboard. The Defence Ministry said the cause of the S-70 crash had not yet been determined. Television footage showed the wreckage burning close to buildings, and flames reportedly reached a nearby house, though no civilian casualties were reported. Police, firefighters and medical teams were sent to the scene.

actors.why: Four military personnel killed in helicopter crash; cause still undetermined

impact_points: Turkey's armed forces lose four personnel, with the ministry offering condolences to grieving families.
The incident is a domestic military loss with no direct international dimension reported in the article.

auto-c7914652672e.headline: Kyiv-linked drone firm UForce secures $700 million at $6 billion valuation
auto-c7914652672e.summary: UForce, a defense technology company with Ukrainian roots and headquarters in London, has raised $700 million in a Series A round that values it at $6 billion. The company says the funds will expand its unmanned systems production for Ukraine and allied countries. The round was co-led by Valor Equity Partners in the United States and the UK's National Wealth Fund, with the U.S.-Ukraine Reconstruction Investment Fund also taking part. The company plans production growth in the US, Europe, Asia-Pacific and the Middle East.

actors.why: Gains investment, hiring and production capacity for drone operations at home.
Hosts UForce headquarters and gains jobs from the National Wealth Fund's record investment.
Gains a US production partnership and investment via Valor and the reconstruction fund.

impact_points: Ukraine stands to gain jobs, research and production capacity as UForce expands its operations there.
The UK and US gain industrial investment, with the UK's National Wealth Fund pledging 113 million pounds and expecting hundreds of skilled jobs.

auto-43e6e4c62959.headline: Kyiv asks Washington to explain alleged Starshield speed limits
auto-43e6e4c62959.summary: Ukraine's government has asked the United States to explain reported speed caps on Starshield, the military version of the Starlink satellite network. Zelensky said the limits, set at about 161 km/h, were disrupting Ukrainian forces, especially over Russian-occupied areas and the front line, and that they hindered interceptors from reaching Shahed-type drones. SpaceX rejected the claim, calling it false and saying nothing had changed. Ukrainian officials and a US congressional caucus have pressed for full restoration of access.

actors.why: Interceptors and communications reportedly hobbled, letting Russian strikes succeed
Accused by Kyiv and lawmakers over Starshield control, though SpaceX denies changes
Reportedly benefits as Ukrainian drone interception and evasion become harder

impact_points: Ukraine's military faces weaker drone defences and communications if the Starshield limits are real.
The United States faces pressure from Kyiv and lawmakers over its control of the militarized terminals.

auto-a4d85396a3f1.headline: Insurance premiums for Russian data centres jump sharply amid drone strikes
auto-a4d85396a3f1.summary:
Insurance for data centres in Russia has become far more expensive, according to the business daily Kommersant, as reported by Meduza. Premiums in the first half of 2026 ran at 0.03 to 0.06 percent of insured value, but have since climbed to between 1 and 5 percent, with some increases exceeding a hundredfold. The shift followed Ukrainian drone strikes in October on facilities operated by Yandex, Sberbank and VK, after earlier Russian attacks on data centres in Ukraine.

The state-owned National Reinsurance Company, owned by the central bank, tightened its terms in October, setting a 1 percent base rate and reviewing certain sites case by case. Experts say insurers are cutting coverage or excluding some risks.

actors.why: Data centre operators face sharply higher insurance costs and reduced coverage after strikes.
Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian data centres are the cause of the rising premiums.

impact_points: Russia's tech firms such as Yandex, Sberbank and VK face higher costs and thinner protection against drone damage.
Russia's central bank-owned reinsurer and insurance market are tightening terms, leaving operators more exposed to attacks.

auto-cac125387f49.headline: Indonesia's vice president resigns amid credential dispute and strained presidential alliance
auto-cac125387f49.summary:
Indonesia's Vice-President Gibran Rakabuming Raka has submitted his resignation to parliament, which will now begin choosing a replacement within 60 days from two candidates named by President Prabowo Subianto. The move followed a Supreme Court ruling that a high-school document he used in the 2024 campaign was invalid, a decision that had fueled impeachment calls. His exit also reflects a cooling relationship between Prabowo and his predecessor and Gibran's father, Joko Widodo, as the government faces other pressures.

Prabowo said he accepted the resignation reluctantly and defended his son's qualifications, arguing that foreign education systems differ from Indonesia's. Jokowi said the move was part of political dynamics and that the post had always been temporary.

actors.why: Vice-presidential vacancy and fractured ruling alliance create domestic political turmoil

impact_points: Indonesia's government must now fill the vice-presidency, adding to political turbulence under President Prabowo.
Jokowi's political standing and his alliance with Prabowo appear weakened, while the replacement choice will shape the balance of power.

auto-04e83365189d.headline: US envoys press Putin and Zelensky on Ukraine peace as Starlink access falters
auto-04e83365189d.summary: US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met Vladimir Putin in Moscow, a day after Ukraine peace talks in Abu Dhabi ended, and then travelled to Dublin to meet Ukrainian President Zelensky. Witkoff said another trilateral round with Putin had been agreed and that European partners would join. Zelensky reported renewed restrictions on Starshield, the military-grade Starlink service, which he said hampered Ukraine's ability to intercept Russian drones. Putin insisted on the state border as the only dividing line and proposed local humanitarian ceasefires, while the wider debate centres on European security arrangements.

actors.why: Starshield restrictions hamper drone interception and Kyiv's territorial position is pressed
Talks continue and Moscow's position on territory and borders remains firm
Envoys lead mediation efforts, though the reporting highlights Ukrainian concerns about US commitments
European states are set to join talks but risk being sidelined on European security arrangements

impact_points: Ukraine faces restricted satellite communications on the front line, weakening its ability to counter Russian drones.
Russia keeps its territorial demands, while European states risk being sidelined from talks on their own security order.

auto-bbb98b156876.headline: Israeli strike hits Gaza's Nasser hospital, killing six, including a surgeon
auto-bbb98b156876.summary: An overnight Israeli air strike on Nasser hospital in Khan Younis, southern Gaza, killed six people and wounded about 30, according to the Hamas-run health ministry. The hospital's director said two missiles struck a surgical building, with one failing to detonate. Among the dead was surgeon Dr Rizq Abu Shaira. The Israeli military said it targeted a Hamas brigade commander and fighters it accused of using the complex as a base. Hamas rejected those claims, and the hospital said it received no warning. Independent verification was not possible, as Israel bars international media from Gaza.

actors.why: Civilians, medics and patients killed in strike on hospital complex
Military says it targeted Hamas commander; faces war crime allegations

impact_points: Gaza's health system, already strained, loses staff and capacity serving nearly one million people in the south.
Israel faces renewed accusations of targeting medical facilities, while Hamas and its civilian population bear the human toll.

auto-c88c2b39bc01.headline: EU's Kallas says Russia is trying to divert attention from Ukraine aggression
auto-c88c2b39bc01.summary: The EU's foreign policy chief, Kaja Kallas, warned European leaders at a Dublin summit not to fall for Russian tactics in Ukraine peace talks. She said Moscow is trying to open a debate about European security to distract from its own aggression. Russia has revived demands for a sweeping overhaul of European security, which were rejected in 2021. Kremlin and Russian negotiators said they would only consider an expanded format including Europe once Europe's intentions are clear. European leaders, including Germany's chancellor, insist Europe must take part in any talks.

actors.why: Russia's hardline demands are under scrutiny, and Europe's inclusion in talks is conditional.
Ukraine faces a peace process where Europe's role is still contested and a ceasefire is not yet agreed.
The bloc is seeking a single representative and warns against Russian manoeuvres in the talks.
Germany insists on a role in any European delegation and rejects reopening European security architecture.
The UK is seen as important to any European peacekeeping role, though its place in talks is unresolved.

impact_points: Ukraine and European states face pressure over security arrangements that Moscow is trying to reopen in the talks.
European countries are divided over who should represent Europe, which could weaken their negotiating position.

auto-c6b9e30900c6.headline: Most Ukrainians see little hope of a near-term peace deal with Russia
auto-c6b9e30900c6.summary: Ukrainian strikes reportedly killed at least nine people inside Russia overnight, officials on both sides said. Russian strikes meanwhile hit a hospital in Kyiv and killed at least three people in southern Ukraine. The violence follows a day of intensive shuttle diplomacy in US-led talks aimed at ending the war, now nearing its fifth year. A France 24 correspondent in Kyiv reports that most Ukrainians believe there is no real chance of a peace agreement being reached.

actors.why: Hospital strike in Kyiv and deaths in the south; public sees no peace prospect
Ukrainian strikes killed nine; Moscow under pressure in stalled talks
Leads intensive shuttle diplomacy seeking to end the war
Expected to join peace talks as part of the wider negotiating effort

impact_points: Ukraine faces continued civilian casualties and public pessimism about a negotiated settlement with Russia.
Russia faces casualties from Ukrainian strikes while talks led by the United States continue without a breakthrough.

auto-0984a068557f.headline: US envoys meet Putin and Zelensky as Ukraine peace talks stall
auto-0984a068557f.summary:
US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff met Vladimir Putin in Moscow after talks in Abu Dhabi on ending the war in Ukraine, and then travelled to Dublin to see President Zelensky. Witkoff said a new round of three-way talks with Putin had been agreed and that European partners would take part. Zelensky reported that Ukraine faces renewed restrictions on access to SpaceX's Starshield service, hampering its ability to intercept Russian drones. Putin repeated that the state border must be the sole line of demarcation and proposed local humanitarian truces, while Russia's core positions appear unchanged.

A central theme is a new European security framework, which Ukraine and Europe view with concern given doubts about the current US commitment to the continent.

actors.why: Starlink restrictions hinder drone interception; territorial demands persist
Demands for territory and neutrality unchanged; gains from US engagement
Leads mediation efforts with envoys shuttling between Moscow, Abu Dhabi and Dublin
Excluded from early talks on European security order, though invited to next round
Planned national security adviser participation in Dublin talks was cancelled

auto-3f57cb79c76b.headline: Israeli strike hits Gaza's Nasser hospital, killing six and injuring about 30
auto-3f57cb79c76b.summary:
An overnight Israeli air strike hit Nasser hospital in Khan Younis, in southern Gaza, killing six people and wounding around 30, according to the Hamas-run health ministry. Among the dead was surgeon Dr Rizq Abu Shaira. The hospital's director said two missiles struck a building housing surgical wards and intensive care units, though only one detonated.

The Israeli military said it targeted a commander of Hamas's armed wing and other fighters it accused of using the hospital as a base for planning attacks, and it claimed to have issued advance warnings. The hospital director said no warning was received. Hamas rejected the Israeli account; these claims could not be independently verified because international media are barred from entering Gaza.

actors.why: Civilian medical facility struck, killing staff and patients; health system further damaged
Military strike on a hospital draws accusations of war crimes and international criticism

impact_points: Palestinians in southern Gaza lose a major hospital serving nearly one million people, deepening the health crisis.
Israel faces renewed international scrutiny over strikes on protected medical facilities, while Hamas's use of civilian sites is disputed.

auto-c20fbe7454c0.headline: US envoys carry Ukraine peace efforts between Moscow and Kyiv's side
auto-c20fbe7454c0.summary: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner have been travelling between Dublin and Moscow as they try to broker a peace agreement between Russia and Ukraine. Their work includes meetings with Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Vladimir Putin. The shuttle diplomacy comes after the first direct talks between Russian and Ukrainian delegations in nine months.

actors.why: Zelenskyy meets US envoys seeking a peace deal; outcome remains uncertain.
Putin receives US envoys after first direct talks in nine months.
Envoys Witkoff and Kushner lead efforts to broker a deal, raising US standing.
Dublin serves as a venue for the envoys' meetings and shuttle diplomacy.

impact_points: Ukraine is seeking a negotiated end to the war and relies on US mediation to reach any deal.
Russia faces pressure to engage in talks, while the US is positioning itself as the central broker.

auto-d28c7f9d8a37.headline: Sachs says US cannot win Iran war militarily or via a formal deal
auto-d28c7f9d8a37.summary: In an interview with Mehr News Agency, economist Jeffrey Sachs argued that Donald Trump cannot secure a victory in the Iran conflict either on the battlefield or through a formal agreement. He suggested fighting could stop if Washington lifted its blockade and withdrew without a signed deal, which would reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Sachs also criticised the UN Security Council and European leaders over their handling of the crisis, and called for regional security arrangements independent of outside powers.

actors.why: Blockade and fighting end would keep Iran safe and reopen Hormuz
Sachs says Washington cannot win and should lift blockade

auto-e73123a1edc3.headline: Latvian PM says Russia lacks standing to dictate European security terms
auto-e73123a1edc3.summary: Latvia's prime minister, Andris Kulbergs, told AFP in Dublin that Russia is not in a strong enough position to put new security demands on Europe. His remarks came after Moscow pushed for Europe's wider security framework to be folded into talks on Ukraine, and as Russia reportedly wants to revive demands to roll back NATO. European leaders decided at the Dublin meeting that Britain, France, Germany, Italy, Poland and the EU institutions would represent Europe in any future negotiations. Kulbergs said he doubted Vladimir Putin wants genuine peace in Ukraine, despite a large prisoner exchange agreed in US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi.

Stands to benefit from Western pressure on Russia but faces ongoing war and no ceasefire

Secured agreed European representation at talks and a clearer negotiating role

auto-d305846a344d.headline: Dutch coalition faces collapse after tax row splits prime minister's partners
auto-d305846a344d.summary: Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten was set to meet key coalition partners on Friday in an effort to keep his minority government intact, nine months after it took office. The crisis followed a tax policy deal struck by his D66 party and the CDA with the opposition left-wing PRO party, which angered the VVD. Its leader, Dilan Yesilgoz, said the coalition would need a fundamental reset, and the VVD voted against the government's own policy after a tax proposal passed parliament narrowly. Jetten's coalition holds only 66 of 150 seats, so an early election, the third in three years, remains possible.

impact_points: The Netherlands faces possible snap elections, with the latest polls favouring the PRO party over the far-right PVV.

auto-2a5959b873f2.headline: US Democratic senators demand Musk keep records on Ukraine Starlink access
auto-2a5959b873f2.summary: Democratic senators have directed Elon Musk to retain records relating to Starlink satellite internet access in Ukraine, according to a Wall Street Journal report carried by Arab News. The move reportedly concerns how Starlink service was provided to Ukrainian users during the war with Russia. The full details of the senators' request could not be verified from the text available here.

Senators are pressing a US company over its wartime Ukraine role
Oversight of Starlink's wartime use could weaken Russia's position in the conflict

impact_points: Ukraine relies on Starlink for connectivity, so scrutiny of its access arrangements matters to Kyiv's communications.
Russia and the US both have stakes in Starlink's role in the conflict, which may draw further political attention.

auto-626e717ecaff.headline: Ukraine reports record Russian casualties as Abu Dhabi peace talks yield limited results
auto-626e717ecaff.summary: Ukraine's military says it inflicted more than 26,000 Russian casualties in the first ten days of November, possibly setting a monthly record, and claims a single-day record of 2,980 on November 9. These figures could not be independently verified. Russia has made little territorial gain this year, according to independent assessments, though its defence ministry claims much larger seizures. At peace talks in Abu Dhabi on November 10-11, Russian negotiator Vladimir Medinsky insisted on terms favouring Moscow, while Ukraine's president Volodymyr Zelenskyy rejected Russia's security proposals. The talks did agree a prisoner exchange of at least 1,000 people per side.

auto-cb2c9a3519a6.headline: ASEAN summit in Manila meets as Trump's Asia trip spotlights tariff strains
auto-cb2c9a3519a6.summary: Southeast Asian leaders are convening in Manila from Sunday to Tuesday for their annual ASEAN summit, with trade expected to dominate. US President Donald Trump plans a brief stop in Manila to meet Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr, then travel to the APEC summit in Shenzhen, China, where he is set to meet Xi Jinping and, for the first time, hold trilateral talks including Russia's Vladimir Putin. New US tariffs of 10 to 12.5 percent on dozens of partners, including most of the region, have so far had limited effect. Analysts warn that electronics exports tied to AI demand could falter, and that future sectoral tariffs or export controls could hit harder.

Hosts APEC and a Trump-Xi-Putin trilateral meeting

Putin set to join first trilateral talks with Trump and Xi

auto-9b7ddb48b5cd.headline: Canada and US report progress toward a trade agreement, says Carney
auto-9b7ddb48b5cd.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said talks between Ottawa and Washington on a trade deal have advanced. The remarks indicate that negotiators have narrowed some differences, though the reporting available does not detail which issues were resolved or when an agreement might be finalised. The update comes amid ongoing tariff tensions between the two neighbours, which have affected cross-border commerce.

auto-30154525a8b5.headline: EU leaders weigh AI growth against risks at Dublin summit
auto-30154525a8b5.summary: EU leaders met in Dublin for their first AI summit, seeking ways to build up Europe's AI sector while keeping the technology safe for citizens. Mistral's chief executive Arthur Mensch and AI researcher Geoffrey Hinton joined the talks. Officials framed the effort as a way to cut the bloc's dependence on foreign technology and to avoid falling further behind the US and China. Attention also turned to a scandal at Nvidia, after its CEO Jensen Huang resigned following reports of extramarital affairs, one involving a woman accused of spying for China. The EU said Nvidia was not formally on the agenda, though it could come up.

Nvidia, a major investor in the EU, faces reputational and security questions after its CEO's resignation and the espionage allegations.

auto-ae949bd3e1c2.headline: Türkiye signs preliminary solar and wind investment deal with China
auto-ae949bd3e1c2.summary: Türkiye has signed a preliminary agreement with China, announced at the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, aimed at drawing roughly $15 billion into solar and wind projects. The deal covers planned farms with a combined capacity of seven gigawatts, plus energy storage and grid upgrades, and includes technology sharing for making wind-turbine equipment in Türkiye. Energy Minister Alparslan Bayraktar announced it, but no timetable or financing details were given. It follows talks between Presidents Erdoğan and Chinese Vice President Han Zheng, who said Beijing would encourage more Chinese firms to invest.

China's companies get new investment opportunities in Türkiye's renewable energy sector, with Beijing pledging to encourage them.

auto-fba706c0ab16.headline: Army seizes arms stash in Beirut suburb, origins unclear
auto-fba706c0ab16.summary:
Lebanon's army raided a warehouse in Musharrafieh, in Beirut's southern suburbs, and confiscated a sizeable quantity of weapons and ammunition. The army said the operation followed surveillance of weapons transport and trafficking, and it detained a Lebanese man identified only by initials, with an investigation under judicial supervision. The warehouse does not appear to belong to Hezbollah, though the raid took place in the group's stronghold. Its owner, reportedly from the Chiyah area, has gone into hiding, and the article says the weapons' origins remain unestablished.

A retired brigadier general said the raid was preemptive and warned that storing ammunition in a densely populated district endangers residents. A military analyst, examining photographs, judged the collection more typical of an experienced dealer than of preparations for combat, and suggested some pistols may have been smuggled from Iraq via Syria, though this could not be confirmed.

actors.why: Army asserts state arms authority, but residents face ammunition storage risks
Some seized pistols possibly smuggled from Iraqi security forces, unverified

impact_points: Lebanon's government faces renewed pressure over its effort to establish a state monopoly on arms.
Hezbollah's stronghold in the southern suburbs is again under scrutiny, while Iraq may be linked to smuggled firearms.

auto-be979cbdf097.headline: Expert says Trump is shifting from war to economic pressure on Iran
auto-be979cbdf097.summary: A US affairs analyst at Israel's Holon Institute of Technology told 103FM radio that President Trump has turned against Vice President JD Vance after the Republican midterm losses. Vance is said to have been sidelined from Iran talks, and Trump reportedly questioned a June memorandum of understanding Vance helped negotiate. The analyst believes Trump will now lean on an economic siege of Tehran rather than renewed military action, and says his window for renewed fighting is narrowing. These are the analyst's own assessments and could not be independently verified.

Vance's critique of Israel's influence and the tilt away from war may affect ties

auto-c91270624cb8.headline: Sudan aid shortfall leaves millions without shelter and food
auto-c91270624cb8.summary: Aid agencies IOM and UNHCR warn that shortfalls in funding have run down emergency shelter and household supplies meant for Sudan. Only about 47 percent of the roughly $2.9 billion needed under the UN response plan has been raised, and only about 10 percent of the 15.4 million people needing shelter and basic items have been reached. Millions remain displaced inside Sudan or in neighbouring countries, while fighting between the army and the paramilitary RSF, drone strikes and access restrictions hamper deliveries. Donors including Germany and the EU are giving less than in previous years, and experts say the true scale of the crisis is hard to measure.

auto-45a51e4288ec.headline: Estonia details drone strike on Russian corvette near Ust-Luga port
auto-45a51e4288ec.summary: Estonian Colonel Aron Kalmus, deputy commander of the Estonian Division, described how several Ukrainian drones hit the Russian Baltic Fleet corvette Naro-Fominsk during a large attack on the Ust-Luga port. He said the vessel was damaged, reportedly with deaths and injuries, and that it could not continue under its own power. Kalmus also said the drones briefly entered Estonian airspace over the Gulf of Finland and southeastern Estonia, too close to the border to be safely shot down. Ukraine's security service earlier said the ship was struck as part of an operation against oil infrastructure at the port.

auto-74598f415c57.headline: Islamic State-linked raiders kill dozens of civilians in eastern Congo
auto-74598f415c57.summary:
Gunmen linked to the Islamic State group killed at least 44 civilians in Ituri province, in the northeast of the Democratic Republic of Congo, during the week, humanitarian and security sources said on Friday. The attacks hit villages in the Mambasa area, roughly 100 kilometres from places where a deadly viral fever was first detected six months ago. Victims were reportedly hacked with machetes or shot, and some bodies were decomposing. Ugandan and Congolese troops have deployed to the region against the Allied Democratic Forces, but have not yet made significant progress.

The violence comes days after the same group killed 66 people in neighbouring North Kivu, where health workers and clinics were attacked during an Ebola outbreak. The epidemic, declared in May, has caused more than 5,400 deaths, the worst in the country's history.

auto-fb79a1f4524f.headline: Houthis pressure Sanaa private schools to join military mobilization rallies
auto-fb79a1f4524f.summary:
Houthi authorities are reportedly pressing private schools in Sanaa and its outskirts to stage at least three student marches and rallies each week, held on school grounds and nearby streets. School sources told Asharq Al-Awsat that the orders cut into lessons and that the group uses annual license renewals as leverage, threatening fines or closure. Several districts' administrators have resisted under pressure from parents who fear for their children's education and the risk of recruitment toward the frontlines. The report links the moves to a recent military escalation in several provinces, including Taiz.

The Houthi-run education ministry has reportedly threatened penalties, while about 170,000 teachers in Houthi-held areas have gone unpaid since 2016.

auto-6caa25448f87.summary: Russian strikes hit multiple targets across Ukraine on Thursday, and one attack damaged a hospital. auto-41e52d23df8c.summary: Tom Cotton, the Republican chair of the US Senate Intelligence Committee, has said further negotiations with Russia to end the war are pointless. auto-a58e70834105.headline: ICC halts probe into US troops in Afghanistan, refocuses on Taliban

auto-a9b7b4a128a8.headline: Russian strike on Odesa energy site leaves about 50,000 homes without power

auto-c594d48b292b.headline: US flights resume after nationwide ground stop from communications outage
